# Invented offer-letter test fixtures

Repository-only software test inputs for Saavdhan's PDF ingest, local OCR,
quote-grounded fallback extraction, rules and verdict pipeline. These are not
employment documents. Every person, organisation, street address, RC number,
signature, email and contact number is invented. Geographic destinations are
test scenarios. No logos, seals or official letterheads are used.

Every page visibly carries this exact label, also used as the PDF metadata Title:

> TEST FIXTURE - invented data for software testing - not a real offer

The scanned PDF includes the label in its pixels and has **no text layer**.

## Generate and test locally

Use the existing project environment; no new dependencies or network access:

```powershell
.venv\Scripts\python tests/fixtures/offers/make_offer_pdfs.py
$env:PYTHON_DOTENV_DISABLED = '1'
$env:SAAVDHAN_ENABLE_LLM = 'false'
$env:OPENAI_API_KEY = ''
$env:LITELLM_API_KEY = ''
.venv\Scripts\python -m pytest tests -q -rx
```

`PYTHON_DOTENV_DISABLED` prevents the application's startup hook from reading
local dotenv files. The generator does not import application startup code.
The tests explicitly disable model extraction and use the real `ingest_bytes`
implementation to build the document and page SourceRefs (including SHA-256),
then call `agent.analyze`. All extracted facts must quote their page source.
The recruiter list is deliberately not loaded: R2 remains unknown and every
verdict carries `ra_list_date = "not loaded"`.

ReportLab and Pillow generate the files. Letter dates are fixed to 12 October
2026; invariant PDF metadata dates are fixed to 1 January 2000 UTC. The scan
uses Pillow's bundled font, a fixed grey noise grid and a 0.35-degree rotation.
There is no randomness. A test requires the complete font-available inventory,
generates two copies and compares every byte with each other and the committed
PDFs under the same installed library/font versions.
Binary Flate streams also prevent Git's Windows line-ending conversion from
altering these PDFs; staged bytes were checked against generated bytes.

## Inventory and expectations

Sizes and observed results below are from the committed files, with local
English Tesseract OCR and the LLM disabled.

| File | Pages | Bytes | Expected verdict | Observed result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| `bangkok_data_entry_offer.pdf` | 1 | 2,240 | STOP | STOP; R7 expectation is a strict xfail |
| `dubai_electrician_offer.pdf` | 2 | 3,076 | VERIFY_FIRST | VERIFY_FIRST; only R4 hits |
| `cambodia_customer_support_scan.pdf` | 1 | 328,779 | STOP | STOP through actual local OCR |
| `laos_it_offer_hindi.pdf` | omitted | — | STOP | Skipped: no permitted Devanagari TTF |
| `saudi_driver_offer_marathi.pdf` | omitted | — | VERIFY_FIRST | Skipped: no permitted Devanagari TTF |

### Bangkok: costly tourist-visa data-entry offer

Tests Thai destination/transit extraction, Indian grouped fee amounts, UPI,
passport handover and urgency. It has an invented Pune correspondence address
and explicitly restricts contact to WhatsApp, with no RC number or mention of
contract signatories, receipt or insurance.

Required hits: `R1_TOURIST_VISA`, `R3_NO_RC_NUMBER`, `R4_FEE_OVER_CAP`,
`R6_HIGH_RISK_CORRIDOR`, `R7_INFORMAL_CHANNEL_ONLY`, `R8_NO_RECEIPT`,
`H2_PASSPORT_HANDOVER`, `H3_PRESSURE`.

Observed hits: `R1_TOURIST_VISA`, `R3_NO_RC_NUMBER`, `R4_FEE_OVER_CAP`,
`R5_NO_TRIPARTITE_CONTRACT`, `R6_HIGH_RISK_CORRIDOR`, `R8_NO_RECEIPT`,
`R9_PBBY_MISSING`, `H1_SALARY_ANOMALY`, `H2_PASSPORT_HANDOVER`, `H3_PRESSURE`.

**Strict xfail:** `test_bangkok_whatsapp_only_contact`. The fallback extractor
recognises the printed correspondence address as `office_address`; R7 then
clears whenever that channel is present, even though contact is expressly
WhatsApp-only. This is a channel-semantics conflict between the requested R7
expectation and the current extractor/rules. Backend code is unchanged. Only
this R7 assertion is xfailed; the STOP verdict, other required hits, labels and
source grounding remain ordinary passing assertions. A future R7 hit produces
a strict XPASS failure requiring review of this mark.

### Dubai: licensed-format electrician offer with excess fee

Tests two-page source attribution, synthetic RC shape, employment visa, AED
salary, accommodation, receipt, pre-departure tripartite contract, insurance,
and a passport that remains with the worker. The invented RC number makes no
claim of actual registration.

Required and observed hit: `R4_FEE_OVER_CAP`. Must not hit:
`R1_TOURIST_VISA`, `R6_HIGH_RISK_CORRIDOR`, `R3_NO_RC_NUMBER`.
VERIFY_FIRST reflects the excess fee and the unloaded recruiter list.

### Cambodia: image-only customer-support offer

Tests the real PDFium-to-Pillow-to-Tesseract path, followed by fallback
extraction. The offer states a visit visa, a cash deposit, Telegram-only
contact and pressure to confirm today.

Required hits: `R1_TOURIST_VISA`, `R6_HIGH_RISK_CORRIDOR`.

Observed hits: `R1_TOURIST_VISA`, `R3_NO_RC_NUMBER`, `R4_FEE_OVER_CAP`,
`R5_NO_TRIPARTITE_CONTRACT`, `R6_HIGH_RISK_CORRIDOR`,
`R7_INFORMAL_CHANNEL_ONLY`, `R8_NO_RECEIPT`, `R9_PBBY_MISSING`, `H3_PRESSURE`.

The structure test always verifies the absence of a text layer. Verdict and
rule tests skip when Tesseract is missing; when available, they also require
the exact footer label in OCR output. OCR ran successfully for this snapshot.

### Hindi and Marathi files

The generator embeds the Nirmala UI Devanagari face from `C:/Windows/Fonts/Nirmala.ttc`
(collection index 0). Both files are committed and both scenarios are tested:

- `laos_it_offer_hindi.pdf`: Hindi IT support in Laos, tourist visa, fee in Hindi
  words, UPI, no receipt, immediate confirmation. Expected STOP with
  `R1_TOURIST_VISA`, `R4_FEE_OVER_CAP`, `R6_HIGH_RISK_CORRIDOR`.
- `saudi_driver_offer_marathi.pdf`: Marathi driver in Riyadh, employment visa, SAR
  salary, Rs 25,000 + GST, receipt, tripartite contract and insurance. Expected
  VERIFY_FIRST solely because the recruiter list is unloaded, with no rule hits.

## Validation snapshot

- Generator completed; repeat generation was byte-identical.
- pypdf opened all three PDFs; Title, fixed date metadata, page counts and
  text-layer requirements passed. Every generated page was rendered and
  visually reviewed, including the scan's visible English footer.
- Full suite: see the run summary in the commit; no skips. One strict xfail: the Bangkok
  WhatsApp-only case, where a printed Pune address makes R7 clear (a rule-semantics question).
- `npm.cmd run build`: TypeScript passed; Vite's default config bundler failed
  because esbuild could not read a parent directory (access denied). Running
  `node node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js build --configLoader runner` passed using
  Vite's built-in alternate loader. No dependencies or configuration changed.
- No backend, dependency manifests, configuration or other tracked files were
  changed. No dotenv files were read and no network calls were made.
